title: Boss: the cafe question
summary: Load, profile, compute and report an answer from raw CSV text.

steps.title: The brief
body: The cafe owner asks: **which item brings in the most money?** You get the till export as CSV text:
a `receipt` number (with leading zeros), `item`, `qty` and `price`, with a few gaps. This is the cafe data the
Work through the workflow: load it with the right types, profile it, compute revenue per item with whole-column
operations, and write a headline the owner can act on. Each step builds on the last; keep your earlier functions.

steps.title: Load it right
steps.prompt: Write `load(text)` that reads the CSV text into a DataFrame with `receipt` kept as text (`"0001"`, not `1`).

steps.title: Profile it
prompt: Add `profile(df)` returning `{"rows": ..., "missing": {column: count}, "items": ...}`: the row count, the
missing values of each column that has any, and the number of distinct items. Plain `int`s only.
solution: "missing": {col: int(n) for col, n in df.isna().sum().items() if n > 0},

steps.title: Revenue per item
prompt: Add `revenue_by_item(df)` returning a dict `{item: revenue}` (rounded to 2 decimals, plain floats), in the order
items first appear among the kept rows:
- Compute a revenue column with one vectorised multiplication, then sum it per item with a boolean mask.
solution: "missing": {col: int(n) for col, n in df.isna().sum().items() if n > 0},
return {item: round(float(revenue[clean["item"] == item].sum()), 2) for item in clean["item"].unique()}

steps.title: The headline
prompt: Add `headline(df)` that prints the answer for the owner:
Latte brings in the most revenue: 10.50 of 24.75 (42%).
2 receipts with missing values were left out.
The total is the sum of the per-item revenue; the percentage has no decimals. The second line counts the rows
dropped for a missing `qty` or `price`, and always says `receipts` (even for 0 or 1).
solution: "missing": {col: int(n) for col, n in df.isna().sum().items() if n > 0},
return {item: round(float(revenue[clean["item"] == item].sum()), 2) for item in clean["item"].unique()}
